beliefs: For x >= 1: f(x) = x^3 + 2^x + 22 exactly, verified at integers, half-integers, and non-integers up to x=128 [E7, E9, E13, E14, E15, E16, E17]
For x <= 0: f(x) = x^3 + 2^x + 22 exactly, verified at integers, half-integers, and non-integers down to x=-128 [E13, E14, E15, E16, E17]
On the open interval (0,1): f(x) = x^3 + 2^x + 22 + g(x) where g is a large negative dip, not a constant -1 [E5, E6, E11, E16, E17]
The (0,1) dip g(x) is roughly -1 near x=0.01 and x=0.99, but reaches about -44 near x=0.5 (f(0.5)=-19.9553 vs base 22.54) [E5, E6, E11, E16]
At the endpoints x=0 and x=1 the base formula nearly holds (f(0)=21.28 vs 23, f(1)=70.35 vs 25 — x=1 is anomalous too?) [E5, E13, E16]?
The dip g(x) appears to have a sharp V or cusp shape peaking near x=0.5, with g(0.02)≈-2.7, g(0.05)≈-6.6, g(0.08)≈-9.6, g(0.12)≈-12.6, g(0.15)≈-13.6 [E17]
The base formula x^3+2^x+22 does NOT hold at large |x| (|x|>~22): observed values are much smaller than 2^x would give [E1, E8, E10]?
At large |x| the function looks polynomial-like (odd, roughly cubic) rather than exponential [E8, E10]?
notes: E17 shows the (0,1) dip is not a constant -1 but a smooth symmetric dip reaching ~-44 at x=0.5, with values ~-2.7 at 0.02 and ~-13.6 at 0.15. I replaced the constant -1 with a fitted symmetric dip function and kept the base formula outside (0,1) since E13-E17 confirm it there.
